Shows the phone\'s own CPU and GPU load over the game, read from the process and the Adreno driver. The performance overlay above reports emulated load; this one tells you whether the device is CPU- or GPU-bound. Applies on the next launch.

The PS3\'s SPU floats are not quite IEEE. Accurate emulates that properly and is slower — needed by games whose SPU code depends on the exact results, such as Skate\'s video decoder.
How much SPU code is compiled at once. Larger blocks run faster but are less compatible; Safe is the reliable choice.
Emulates SPU memory transfers precisely. Costly, and only a handful of games need it.
Keeps rendered frames readable by the game. Fixes missing effects and black or garbled screens in some titles, at a performance cost.
Turns off rendering shortcuts. Noticeably slower, but clears up some visual glitches.
Not a valid adrenotools driver package.

None yet — add one with Menu → Scan folder on the library screen.
Off (default): the game\'s own aspect ratio is kept, with black bars. On: the image is stretched to fill the display.

Three quick steps. Every one of them can wait — you can change all of this later in Settings.
Install PS3UPDAT.PUP, downloadable from Sony\'s site. Homebrew runs without it.
Point at your ISO / game-folder library. Games are scanned in place — nothing is copied.
Turnip is recommended on Adreno. The system driver works out of the box.
Skip for now — homebrew runs without firmware, and everything here lives in Settings later.
Auto hides the touch controls as soon as a physical controller is used.
Takes effect after restarting the app. Turnip recommended on Adreno.

Draws the emulator\'s own counters over the game. Useful for telling a game that is genuinely running at full speed from one that only looks like it. It is not free: the text is drawn through the same overlay path as the emulator\'s dialogs, and the higher detail levels walk every PPU and SPU thread a few times a second. Turn it off once you have your answer.

More detail costs more to collect. Minimal is the frame rate alone. Low adds total CPU load. Medium splits that load into PPU, SPU and RSX. High also shows frame time in milliseconds, the number of PPU/SPU/total threads, and how busy the RSX thread is. None hides the text but still draws any graphs below.
Where the counters sit. Move them if they cover something the game draws in that corner.

Plots the last 50 frame-rate samples under the counters, with the minimum, maximum, average and worst one-percent. Shows whether a number is steady or an average of good and bad stretches. Adds another drawn element per frame.

Plots the last 170 individual frame times. Spikes here are the stutters you feel but that an averaged frame rate hides. The most expensive option on this screen — it samples on every frame, not on the update interval.
Positional puts Cross on the bottom on Nintendo-labeled pads (the Thor\'s built-in controller). Ignored once a custom mapping is saved.
How visible the touch controls are over the game.
Scales every touch control. Applies on the next game start.
Tap a control, then press the physical button to bind it. Sticks and analog triggers map automatically.
Press a button on your controller…\n(Back on the touchscreen cancels)
Downloads box covers from GameTDB and the RPCS3 community compatibility list (the colored dot on each game). Matched by serial — nothing about your library is uploaded.
Optional online data: box covers courtesy of GameTDB.com (non-commercial); compatibility statuses courtesy of the RPCS3 community compatibility list at rpcs3.net.
CellStation is an unofficial Android port of RPCS3 (GPL-2.0), not affiliated with or supported by the RPCS3 team. No firmware or game content is included.
